title: Identify X, Y and Z - chlorine, nitrogen trichloride and chlorine trifluoride: structure and uses
summary: Three unknowns hidden in a chain of reactions. Press start and the lab does the rest: MnO2 and concentrated HCl give a greenish-yellow gas that a colour chart and an atom balance identify as Cl2; Cl2 in excess turns NH3 into NCl3 one H at a time; Cl2 and excess F2 at 573 K give ClF3. Each product is built in 3D, its shape worked out by VSEPR, and every option is tested claim - evidence - verdict before the answer is revealed. No prediction stage - input, run, watch, result.
subject: Chemistry
topic: Chlorine, nitrogen trichloride and interhalogens - preparation, structure and uses
subtopics: Preparation of chlorine: MnO2 + conc. HCl
Reaction of chlorine with ammonia - excess Cl2 gives NCl3, excess NH3 gives N2 and NH4Cl
VSEPR shapes: trigonal pyramidal NCl3, T-shaped ClF3
Lewis basicity and the -I effect of substituents
Uses of chlorine and of ClF3
concepts: X is the greenish-yellow gas from MnO2 + 4HCl -> MnCl2 + Cl2 + 2H2O; atom balance leaves exactly two Cl atoms for X, so X = Cl2
Chlorine is used for sterilising drinking water - (A) true
With Cl2 in excess every N-H of NH3 is replaced: NH3 + 3Cl2 -> NCl3 + 3HCl, so Y = NCl3
NCl3 has 3 bond pairs and 1 lone pair on N: tetrahedral electron geometry, trigonal pyramidal molecule - not planar, (B) false
Cl (3.16) is more electronegative than N (3.04) and H (2.20) is less; the chlorines withdraw density from N, so NCl3 is a weaker Lewis base than NH3 - (D) false
Cl2 + 3F2 -> 2ClF3 at 573 K with F2 in excess, so Z = ClF3: 3 bond pairs + 2 lone pairs, T-shaped
ClF3 fluorinates uranium to UF6 (U + 3ClF3 -> UF6 + 3ClF), the volatile compound used in the enrichment of 235U - (C) true
formulas: steric number = bond pairs + lone pairs; lone pairs = (valence electrons - bonds) / 2
answerValue: X = Cl2, Y = NCl3, Z = ClF3

derivedQuantities.custom_excess_NH3: Y = N2 + NH4Cl - question pathway not followed
derivedQuantities.custom_F2_not_excess_or_473K: Z = ClF - question pathway not followed

methods: Solved independently before any key was consulted: X = Cl2 from the colour and the atom balance; Y = NCl3 with Cl2 in excess; Z = ClF3 with F2 in excess at 573 K; (A), (C)
Element conservation (sympy): MnO2 + aHCl -> MnCl2 + X + bH2O leaves X with no Mn, O or H and exactly two Cl atoms (a = 4, b = 2)
Every equation used on the page balances, including the stepwise NH3 -> NH2Cl -> NHCl2 -> NCl3 substitution, the excess-NH3 route to N2 + NH4Cl, ClF and U + 3ClF3 -> UF6 + 3ClF
VSEPR electron counting: NCl3 4 pairs (1 lone) trigonal pyramidal; ClF3 5 pairs (2 lone, equatorial) T-shaped
Geometry: measured N-Cl 1.759 A and Cl-N-Cl 107.1 deg put N 0.65 A above the Cl3 plane; an RDKit 3D embedding agrees
Lewis basicity: Pauling electronegativities; Hartree-Fock/6-31G* (pyscf) proton affinity NH3 909 vs NCl3 744 kJ/mol, N charge -1.02 vs -0.58, both molecules treated identically
Uses from NCERT Class 12 (p-Block Elements): chlorine sterilises drinking water; ClF3 makes UF6 for the enrichment of 235U
Independent script tests/verify_p1q06.py: 37 of 37 checks pass
Solution websites: MathonGo's published solution (their Q38) gives (A), (C) with the same identifications
The page identifies X, Y and Z with its own reaction engine and evaluates each printed statement on the identified compounds at run time

Headless-browser suite tests/sim_p1q06.js drives the whole page: the engine and its custom-condition branches, the optional conditions and their warnings, the automatic nine-stage run from one START, the answer panel messages, the live data, the option board and badges, the reasoning log, the reveal and its blink, the molecular explorer (drag, keys, compare), replay, pause, reset, KMnO4 and excess-NH3 custom runs, classroom mode, 390 and 360 px, reduced motion, the feed entries, and the real app shell opening it

interactivity: Mission brief with the three reactions and X = ?, Y = ?, Z = ? tiles that fill in as each compound is identified
Station 1: flask, HCl, burner, delivery tube and gas jar filling with greenish-yellow gas; a colour chart and an atom-balance ledger identify X; a water-treatment demonstration for (A)

Station 2: stepwise substitution NH3 -> NH2Cl -> NHCl2 -> NCl3 with HCl leaving; the NCl3 pyramid in 3D with its side view (N 0.65 A above the Cl3 plane, PLANAR? NO); NH3 vs NCl3 lone-pair comparison for (D)
Station 3: a chamber heated to 573 K with excess F2, ClF3 molecules forming; the T-shape inside its trigonal-bipyramid guide; a conceptual U -> UF6 -> 235U enrichment flow for (C)
An option analysis board: claim, evidence and verdict for each of (A)-(D)
